images.title: A three row number pyramid
images.purpose: Shows the pyramid rule: each box is the sum of the two boxes directly below it.
images.composition: Six square boxes stacked as a pyramid in the centre: three in the bottom row, two above, one on top.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Bottom row of three equal square boxes side by side with teal (#0072B2) outlines holding 1, 9 and 4 from left to right. Middle row of two equal boxes with amber (#E69F00) outlines, each centred over the join of the two bottom boxes below it, holding 10 and 13. One top box with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline, centred over the middle row, holding 23. Six boxes in all, white fill, dark numerals, no arrows, no other marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Each box is the sum of the two boxes below it.
images.description: Shows the pyramid rule: each box is the sum of the two boxes directly below it.
images.context: Opening picture for building pyramids upward (1 + 9 = 10, 9 + 4 = 13, 10 + 13 = 23).

image_decisions.why: The pyramid rule is a picture: seeing 1 and 9 under 10, 9 and 4 under 13, and 10 and 13 under 23 shows it at once.
